records.summary: 2351 Mission St operates as an existing restaurant with an active ABC Type 47 license (issued October 2019), and the records confirm restaurant use here since at least 1998. The property lies in the Mission Street NCT zoning district where restaurants are a conditional use, and sits within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District—however, the SUD permits restaurants operating as bona fide eating places to serve alcohol, and the district allows license transfers. The immediate block is dense with food and beverage businesses: 19 registered establishments within 500 ft, 11 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, and 46 licenses within 1,000 ft. The project adds outdoor seating with alcohol service to an existing licensed restaurant, which the pathway rules read as no change of use.

patterns.pattern: Existing restaurant uses on Mission Street NCT are routinely approved as continuations via agency referrals (Miscellaneous Permits) in 7–36 days without Planning Commission hearings, citing Planning Code Section 754 which makes restaurants a permitted conditional use in NCT-Mission.

Within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD, Planning imposes a condition that restaurants must operate as Bona Fide Eating Places, consistent with the SUD requirement that alcohol service be incidental to meals.

The one outdoor seating precedent on this corridor (2323 Mission St, 73 m away) required a full Conditional Use Authorization from the Planning Commission, not an agency referral, and took 9 months to approve. This suggests outdoor seating additions may be treated as discretionary changes requiring a public hearing.

Type 47 full-bar licenses for existing restaurants in NCT-Mission are approved by Planning as continuations via agency referrals in 7–10 days, without hearings, when tied to an established restaurant use.

Restaurant legalizations in NCT-Mission that went through full Conditional Use Authorization hearings (not continuations) were approved with standard eating and drinking conditions: sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius, noise and odor controls, garbage containment inside, and appointment of a community liaison.

Accessory or expansion uses at existing restaurants on this Mission Street block (e.g., commissary/catering) have been approved administratively in 10 days without discretionary review, treated as minor modifications to established uses.

Planning has explicitly recognized that 2351 Mission St contains both a restaurant use and a parking facility use as separate uses on the same lot; the 2018 approval noted the restaurant is 'separate from parking facility use on lot.'

findings.text: An active ABC Type 47 license (on-sale general, eating place) has been on file at 2351 Mission St since October 31, 2019, held by Down With This Sort of Thing LLC.

The restaurant at 2351 Mission St was noted by Planning in September 2018 as separate from the parking facility use on the same lot, confirming two distinct uses on the parcel.

A prior Conditional Use Authorization (case 2014.0704C, decided August 2014) is on file at this address for a formula retail use, and the proposal does not state whether it changes any condition of that earlier approval.

A Conditional Use Authorization at 2323 Mission St (73 m away, same zoning) approved outdoor seating at a bar/restaurant in December 2017 after a Planning Commission hearing; that case took 268 days from filing to approval.

Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District § 249.60(d) requires expanded liquor establishments to provide outside lighting, limit window signage to 33%, and maintain 50% clear street-facing glazing, in addition to § 202.2 operating conditions.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule a pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning to determine whether the outdoor seating addition requires Conditional Use Authorization or qualifies under Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Explain that Casements is an existing restaurant at 2351 Mission St with a Type 47 license since 2019, last approved by Planning in December 2019 as a Bona Fide Eating Place. The proposal is to add outdoor seating in the parking lot on the same parcel, with alcohol service. Ask whether this is read as enlarging a conditional use under § 178, whether the Mission SUD expansion rule in § 249.60(c)(3) applies to a Bona Fide Eating Place, and whether the outdoor area can proceed under § 202.2(a)(7) if it operates 9 a.m.–10 p.m. with seated service only and alcohol dispensed inside or by wait staff. Confirm in writing before filing.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms Conditional Use is required, file a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning, including a project description, site plan showing the outdoor area, and a statement of compliance with Mission SUD § 249.60(d) design requirements.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Frame the outdoor seating as an accessory expansion of the existing restaurant use on the same parcel, with alcohol service subordinate to meals consistent with the Bona Fide Eating Place requirement. Commit to operating hours ending by 10 p.m. (or the time confirmed with Planning), seated service only with no standing, and alcohol dispensed inside or by wait staff at patrons' outdoor seats. Address good-neighbor policies: sidewalk maintenance within one block, noise and odor controls, indoor garbage containment, and a designated community liaison. Provide outside lighting, limit window signage to 33%, and maintain 50% clear glazing per § 249.60(d).

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms the outdoor area qualifies under § 202.2(a)(7) and no Conditional Use is required, submit a health permit application to San Francisco Department of Public Health for the outdoor seating expansion.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the outdoor area meets all § 202.2(a)(7) limits: ground level, hours 9 a.m.–10 p.m., not operated in association with a Bar use, seated areas only with no standing, and alcohol dispensed only inside the premises or by wait staff at the patron's outdoor seat. DPH will route the application to Planning for zoning review under the Interagency Permit Referrals process; Planning will confirm the outdoor area is permitted.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for a health permit to operate with the expanded outdoor seating area from San Francisco Department of Public Health, Environmental Health Branch.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the application online with the Business Account Number (BAN), Location ID (LIN), and federal tax ID. Confirm that a certified food safety manager is on staff (required before the permit is issued). Schedule a pre-opening inspection at least two weeks in advance once the outdoor area is ready. The outdoor seating is an expansion of the existing restaurant use approved in December 2019.

filing_playbook.action: If a building permit is required for outdoor construction (furniture, railings, or changes to the parking lot surface), file a building permit application with San Francisco Department of Building Inspection, routed to Planning under § 175(a).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the outdoor seating area is in the parking lot on the same parcel as the existing restaurant at 2351 Mission St. If Conditional Use was obtained, cite the CUA case number and attach the approval. If proceeding under § 202.2(a)(7), state that the outdoor area meets all limits and no discretionary approval was required. Provide site plans and construction drawings. Planning will review for zoning compliance.

timeline_cost.notes: No time or cost range is given because the entitlement pathway is not established. The zoning row says further review is required: enlarging the existing restaurant triggers Conditional Use under Planning Code §§ 178 and 249.60(c)(3), and whether the outdoor area meets the § 202.2(a)(7) limits (which would allow it as of right) is not established. If Conditional Use is required, expect 4–10 months including pre-application meeting, environmental review, Planning Commission hearing, and appeal period. The one comparable outdoor seating CUA at 2323 Mission St (73 m away) took 268 days. If the outdoor area qualifies under § 202.2(a)(7), the health permit (14–45 days, $470–$1,000) is the primary step. A pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning is required to settle the pathway before any time or cost estimate can be given.
